candidates.question:
In triangle $ABC$, $D$ is on $[AB]$ and $E$ is on $[AC]$ with $DE \parallel BC$.
$|AD| = 4$ cm, $|DB| = 2$ cm and $|DE| = 6$ cm.
Find $|BC|$.

lines.text: $DE \parallel BC$, so $|\angle ADE| = |\angle ABC|$ (corresponding angles). Angle $A$ is common.
Triangles $ADE$ and $ABC$ are equiangular, so they are similar.

steps.title: Write the ratio of corresponding sides (Theorem 13)

lines.text: $D \leftrightarrow B$ and $E \leftrightarrow C$, so $[DE]$ corresponds to $[BC]$ and $[AD]$ to $[AB]$.

steps.title: Match corresponding sides of the similar triangles

lines.text: $A$ matches $D$, $B$ matches $B$, $D$ matches $C$, so $[AB]$ matches $[DB]$ and $[BD]$ matches $[BC]$.
$y$ is a length, so it is positive.

steps.title: Find two pairs of equal angles

lines.text: $PA \parallel BR$, so $|\angle HBQ| = |\angle HAP|$. Reason: alternate angles.
$|\angle QHB| = |\angle PHA|$. Reason: vertically opposite angles.
Two angles are equal, so $\triangle AHP$ and $\triangle BHQ$ are equiangular, hence similar.

steps.title: Write the ratio of corresponding sides

lines.text: $A \leftrightarrow B$ and $H \leftrightarrow H$, so $AH$ corresponds to $BH$ and $AP$ corresponds to $BQ$.
Corresponding sides of similar triangles are proportional: $\dfrac{|AH|}{|HB|} = \dfrac{|AP|}{|QB|}$.
Multiply both sides by $|HB|\,|QB|$: $|AH| \times |QB| = |AP| \times |HB|$.

candidates.question:
In triangle $ABC$, $|AB| = 15$ cm, $|BC| = 20$ cm and $|AC| = 25$ cm.
Find $\angle ABC$.

lines.text: $|AB|^2 + |BC|^2 = |AC|^2$, so by the converse of Pythagoras the angle opposite $|AC|$ is a right angle.

candidates.question:

lines.text: By the converse of Pythagoras, the triangle has a right angle between the sides of length 5 and 12.
The two shorter sides are perpendicular, so they are the base and the height.

steps.title: Write the area using the $9$ m side as base

candidates.question:
In triangle $ABC$, $|BC| = 10$ cm and the perpendicular distance from $A$ to $BC$ is $6$ cm.
$|AC| = 8$ cm.
Find the perpendicular distance from $B$ to $AC$.

lines.text: Area is half the base times the perpendicular height.
By Theorem 16, base × height is the same for every side, so the area is the same using $[AC]$ as base. Let $h$ be the height from $B$.
